title: A Lantern for the Harbor
premise: In the winter of a collapsing republic, courier Dominic Winterbourne carries diplomatic codes aboard a crowded evacuation ship bound for a neutral harbor, hiding among sailors and refugees to stay unnoticed. A stranger boards with letters written in the unmistakable hand of Dominic's presumed-dead sister, revealing she survived the purge and is bargaining for a berth on his ship. As factions aboard fight over the last seats of power—and the codes that could legitimize a government-in-exile—Dominic must decide whether to spend his one favor saving his sister, the orphaned boy he has come to love, or the old archivist who holds the republic's memory. He gives the berth to the boy, sends his sister the codes instead of himself, and stays behind as the lantern of the harbor watch—finding that family is not who you save, but who you choose to remain with.
about_author: H. M. Vane is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from evacuated port cities. Writing from a coastal town that has twice changed flags, Vane specializes in quiet histories of people caught between loyalty and survival.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, works as a deckhand aboard the evacuation ship Meridian, hiding his courier's satchel among tar and rope. He observes the desperate passengers boarding and reflects on the republic's fall. Emotional beat: guarded anonymity, the comfort of useful hands.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Departing
chapters.summary: Through quartermaster Odile's POV, the passenger list reveals names that should be dead. Dominic recognizes one and burns his copy. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Hand He Knew
chapters.summary: A stranger named Corvane boards at the last port, carrying letters in Dominic's sister Lys's handwriting—the sister executed two years past. Dominic, POV, must decide whether to reveal himself. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: What the Codes Are Worth
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, deciphers the first layer of his diplomatic codes and realizes they can legitimize a government-in-exile—making him the most dangerous man aboard. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of power he never wanted.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Hold
chapters.summary: Tobias, a stowaway orphan, POV. He hides among cargo and is caught by Dominic, who feeds him instead of reporting him. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness, the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV, reveals he was Lys's fellow prisoner and offers passage to her in exchange for the codes. Emotional beat: seduction and suspicion entwined.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: Odile, POV, navigates the ship through a winter gale while factions among the passengers begin organizing—loyalists, profiteers, and exiles. Emotional beat: fragile order under pressure.

chapters.title: Letters Never Burned
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, reads Lys's letters in full and learns she survived by informing on friends, including the archivist Merrick now aboard. Emotional beat: love complicated by shame.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Room
chapters.summary: Merrick, POV, tends the ship's small library of rescued state papers and quietly tests Dominic's loyalty with questions about memory and duty. Emotional beat: intellectual intimacy, a second kind of family.

chapters.title: Mutiny in Miniature
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV, witnesses passengers steal rations and a knife fight in the hold; he warns Dominic, proving his worth. Emotional beat: the boy earning his place.

chapters.title: The Neutral Harbor Refuses
chapters.summary: Odile, POV: the destination port closes its gates to the ship, citing the codes as contraband. The Meridian must find another harbor or drift. Emotional beat: collective despair, stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Corvane's True Cargo
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV, discovers Corvane is an agent of the new regime, sent to retrieve the codes and silence the ship. Emotional beat: betrayal, the trap closing.

chapters.title: Lantern Watch
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV, is taught the harbor-watch lantern signals by an old sailor—a ritual of guiding others home at one's own post. Emotional beat: belonging, quiet foreshadowing.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Saloon
chapters.summary: Passengers debate surrendering the codes to save the ship; Merrick argues memory must survive even if men do not. Odile, POV. Emotional beat: democracy's dignity in a drowning room.

chapters.title: Sister, at a Distance
chapters.summary: A smuggled message confirms Lys waits at a fishing village with her own berth secured—if Dominic brings the codes. Dominic, POV. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing into agony.

chapters.title: What Merrick Knew
chapters.summary: Merrick, POV, confesses he knew of Lys's collaboration and stayed silent to protect Dominic. Trust fractures and re-forms. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of family.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: only one seat remains on the escape skiff. He looks at Lys's letter, Tobias's sleeping face, Merrick's failing health. Emotional beat: the novel's central decision, rendered in stillness.

chapters.title: Corvane Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Corvane boards with soldiers under a parley flag; Odile stalls them while Dominic hides the codes inside Merrick's archive. Tobias, POV. Emotional beat: terror and quick, clever courage.

chapters.title: Fire on the Meridian
chapters.summary: Climax: the parley breaks; the ship burns. Dominic gives the berth to Tobias, sends the codes to Lys with Corvane's own dispatch case, and stays to hold the lantern line with Odile and Merrick. Dominic, POV. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Merrick, POV, tends the burned archive and finds the codes' cipher key survived in his memory alone—power reduced to what one mind can carry. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into stewardship.

chapters.title: The Harbor That Took Them In
chapters.summary: A smaller port opens its gates to survivors. Odile, POV, logs the dead and the living with equal care. Emotional beat: exhausted gratitude, community rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: A Lantern for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Dominic's POV: spring. He keeps the harbor light, Tobias studies under Merrick, and a letter arrives from Lys—unopened, then read. He chooses to remain, and the family he built holds. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept burning.
